subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: An advantage of internal recruitment is that:
options: It avoids the need for training
The candidate is already known to the business and it is usually cheaper
It always brings in fresh ideas from outside
It guarantees a larger pool of applicants
questions.explain: Internal recruitment is cheaper and the applicant is already known, though it may limit fresh ideas.

options: Many layers of hierarchy and narrow spans of control
questions.explain: A tall structure has many hierarchical layers, usually with narrow spans of control.

questions.q: Taylor's theory of motivation suggests workers are mainly motivated by:
options: Money and pay linked to output
questions.explain: Taylor argued workers are chiefly motivated by money, e.g. through piece-rate pay linked to output.

questions.q: Why is staff retention important to a business?
options: Retention has no effect on costs
Keeping experienced staff reduces recruitment and training costs
questions.explain: Retaining experienced staff lowers the cost of recruiting and training replacements and keeps knowledge in the firm.

options: Removing one or more layers of management from the hierarchy
questions.explain: Delayering removes layers of management, widening spans of control and shortening the chain of command.

questions.q: According to Maslow, which is a lower-level (basic) need?
options: Physiological needs such as pay for food and shelter
questions.explain: In Maslow's hierarchy, physiological needs (e.g. basic pay) are at the bottom and must be met first.

options: Training given to new employees when they start a job
Always done away from the workplace
questions.explain: Induction training introduces new employees to the business, their role and procedures.

options: Learning while doing the actual job at the workplace
Watching online videos at home only
questions.explain: On-the-job training takes place at the workplace while the employee carries out the job.

questions.q: The recruitment process usually begins with:
options: Identifying a vacancy and producing a job description
questions.explain: Recruitment starts by identifying a vacancy and writing a job description and person specification.

questions.q: In an organisational structure, the 'span of control' is:
options: The number of layers in the hierarchy
The number of employees a manager is directly responsible for
The length of the working day
questions.explain: Span of control is the number of subordinates a manager directly supervises.

questions.q: Which is an example of a non-financial method of motivation?
questions.explain: Job rotation and added responsibility motivate without extra pay, so they are non-financial methods.

options: The leader making all decisions alone
The leader involving employees in decision-making
questions.explain: A democratic leader consults and involves employees when making decisions.
